title: OpenREL Vocabulary — Normalization Decisions and Conceptual Map
description: Documents the modeling decisions, merges, removals, and transformations applied to produce the normalized OpenREL vocabulary from the EOSC-RML_Policy_Snippet_Vocabulary Draft v0.2.

overview.conceptual_basis: Sections 1-90 (90 sections, used as conceptual source only)

key_modeling_decisions.decision: Action normalization: reduce to a core set
key_modeling_decisions.rationale: The draft defined over 200 unique action names, most of which are domain-specific elaborations of a small set of ODRL core actions (use, distribute, modify, archive, delete). Over-specific action naming makes policies incomparable and prevents interoperability. Variations in meaning (commercial vs. non-commercial, anonymized vs. identifiable) belong in constraints, not in action labels.

key_modeling_decisions.decision: Replace boolean constraint values with typed references
key_modeling_decisions.rationale: The draft modelled constraints as '{name: consent, operator: eq, rightOperand: true/false}'. This is not valid in ODRL. Consent is not a boolean: it is a legal classification. The rightOperand must be a typed URI (dpv:Consent) or a typed primitive. 'false' as a prohibition rightOperand is particularly problematic — it inverts the constraint polarity rather than expressing a prohibition directly.
key_modeling_decisions.after: Prohibition with constraint: {leftOperand: dpv:hasLegalBasis, operator: odrl:neq, rightOperand: dpv:Consent, rightOperand_type: xsd:anyURI}

key_modeling_decisions.rationale: The draft used operators 'definesAs', 'isNull', and 'outside' which do not exist in the ODRL specification. These render policies uninterpretable by any ODRL-compliant engine.

replacements.isNull: Dropped — absence of a required endpoint is a policy implementation failure, not a constraint expression. Encode as a prohibition with no-endpoint condition.
replacements.outside: odrl:or of two bounded constraints (lt start OR gt end)

key_modeling_decisions.rationale: The draft contained no agent modelling whatsoever. Every policy lacked assigner and assignee declarations, making it impossible to determine who is granting rights to whom. This is a fundamental gap for machine-actionable policy evaluation. The normalized vocabulary defines 7 canonical agent types and requires that every instantiated policy include at minimum an assigner and an assignee.

key_modeling_decisions.decision: Deduplicate sections expressing the same pattern
key_modeling_decisions.rationale: Multiple sections in the draft (particularly Sections 91-119) expressed identical logic with trivially different values. Deduplication reduces cognitive load and prevents policy drift.

key_modeling_decisions.decision: Replace generic source links with granular references
key_modeling_decisions.rationale: The draft cited 'https://eosc-portal.eu/' across 46+ sections with no article, document, or version specificity. This is not a useful reference for either human readers or machine processing. All sources have been replaced with specific document URIs, article numbers where applicable, and issuer metadata.

key_modeling_decisions.decision: Use DPV for purpose, role, and legal basis expressions
key_modeling_decisions.rationale: The draft used informal strings like 'nonCommercial', 'researchPurpose', 'consent=true'. The Data Privacy Vocabulary (DPV) provides a W3C-maintained taxonomy of purposes (dpv:AcademicResearch, dpv:CommercialResearch), legal bases (dpv:Consent, dpv:LegitimateInterest), and roles (dpv:Researcher, dpv:DataController). Using DPV terms makes policies interoperable with GDPR-aligned systems.

key_modeling_decisions.decision: Model attribution as a duty, not a constraint
key_modeling_decisions.rationale: In CC-REL and ODRL, attribution is an obligation that accompanies a permission — something the assignee must DO, not a condition on the permission itself. The draft inconsistently modelled attribution as both a constraint (rightOperand: false in prohibitions) and a duty action ('provideAttribution'). Normalized to: openrel:attribute as a duty on permissions that permit openrel:distribute.

Sections 1-90 describe policy themes and principles (IPR, personal data, ethics, AI, collaboration) but their JSON is not machine-actionable. The actions, constraints, and sources from these sections have been normalized into the canonical registries. The sections themselves are not preserved as policy entries because they do not specify targets, assigners, assignees, or operational constraints in a resolvable form. They inform the vocabulary design but do not constitute policies.
key_modeling_decisions.preservation: The conceptual themes from Sections 1-90 are mapped in meta/conceptual-map.json and can be used as human-readable policy documentation or as tags on policy instances.

key_modeling_decisions.decision: Compound constraint composition using odrl:and / odrl:or
key_modeling_decisions.rationale: The draft never combined constraints within a single permission rule. Example B (the complex policy) requires simultaneous satisfaction of six constraints. ODRL supports this via odrl:and refinements on the Constraint class. This is the correct pattern for conjunctive policy evaluation. The draft's approach of listing separate policies for each constraint dimension would require a policy enforcement engine to correlate them, which is not guaranteed.

removed_or_not_preserved_as_policies.reason: Not machine-actionable in their current form; narrative/thematic content only
sections: Sections 53-90 (Training, Recruitment, Metrics, Policy, Closing Remarks, etc.)
removed_or_not_preserved_as_policies.note: The actions, sources, and conceptual themes from these sections are captured in the actions, constraints, and sources registries. Only the JSON policy shells are not preserved, because they lack operational specificity.

preserved_unchanged_in_spirit.description: Sections where the core semantics were sound and only operator/typing corrections were needed

cc_rel_integration.description: Creative Commons REL (CC REL) uses permits, prohibits, and requires to express conditions. These map naturally to ODRL permissions, prohibitions, and duties.
cc_rel_integration.compatibility_note: CC licences themselves are not modified by this vocabulary. The CC REL concepts are mapped INTO the ODRL/OpenREL model to enable interoperability with non-CC licensed data. CC-licensed data should continue to use CC licence URIs as the odrl:inheritFrom reference.

odrl_namespace_extensions.rationale: These extensions are necessary because ODRL's core vocabulary does not cover all EOSC-specific requirements (ethics approval, TOM, data volume, revocation status). All extensions are defined in the OpenREL namespace and documented here for pipeline transparency.

meta/.conceptual-map.json: Mapping of Sections 1-90 to vocabulary concepts (future)
meta/.namespace.json: OpenREL namespace declarations and prefix definitions (future)

openrel-vocab/.README.md: Human-readable overview of the vocabulary structure

pipeline_integration.google_sheets_to_json: The constraint registry and policy templates are designed for tabular input. Each constraint entry maps to one spreadsheet row. The policy templates use [INSTANCE] placeholders that can be populated programmatically from a Google Sheet.
pipeline_integration.github_actions: Validation of policies against the ODRL schema can be automated via a GitHub Actions workflow using the odrl-validator tool.
pipeline_integration.identifiers: All IDs use the openrel: prefix with the format openrel:{type}:{category}:{name}. This is stable and URI-resolvable under the openrel.eu domain.
